enriched_entities.name: neurofibromin 1
enriched_entities.function: RAS GTPase-activating protein; tumor suppressor; negative regulator of RAS/MAPK signaling
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Disease gene - loss-of-function mutations cause neurofibromatosis type 1; hyperactive RAS signaling may affect tumor response to chemotherapy

enriched_entities.name: DNA topoisomerase II beta
enriched_entities.function: Catalyzes ATP-dependent transient DNA double-strand breaks; essential for DNA replication, transcription, and chromosome segregation
enriched_entities.role_in_context: PRIMARY TOXICITY MEDIATOR - doxorubicin stabilizes TOP2B-DNA cleavage complexes in cardiomyocytes causing DNA damage and apoptosis leading to cardiotoxicity. Inhibiting TOP2B reduces cardiotoxicity but preserving TOP2A maintains anti-tumor efficacy
enriched_entities.clinical_relevance: TOP2B knockout or inhibition protects against doxorubicin cardiotoxicity in preclinical models

enriched_entities.name: carbonyl reductase 1
enriched_entities.function: NADPH-dependent oxidoreductase; metabolizes carbonyl compounds including anthracyclines
enriched_entities.role_in_context: TOXICITY MEDIATOR - converts doxorubicin to the more cardiotoxic metabolite doxorubicinol (C-13 alcohol); CBR1 inhibition may reduce cardiotoxicity
enriched_entities.clinical_relevance: CBR1 polymorphisms associated with variable doxorubicin cardiotoxicity risk

enriched_entities.name: DNA topoisomerase II alpha
enriched_entities.function: Catalyzes ATP-dependent transient DNA double-strand breaks; highly expressed in proliferating cells
enriched_entities.role_in_context: PRIMARY ANTI-TUMOR TARGET - doxorubicin stabilizes TOP2A-DNA cleavage complexes in rapidly dividing tumor cells causing DNA damage and apoptosis. Preserving TOP2A activity is essential for anti-tumor efficacy
enriched_entities.clinical_relevance: TOP2A expression correlates with anthracycline sensitivity in cancer

enriched_entities.name: glutathione S-transferase mu 1
enriched_entities.function: Phase II detoxification enzyme; conjugates glutathione to electrophilic compounds and reactive oxygen species
enriched_entities.role_in_context: PROTECTIVE - detoxifies doxorubicin-induced reactive intermediates and protects against oxidative stress. GSTM1 null genotype associated with increased doxorubicin toxicity risk
enriched_entities.clinical_relevance: Common GSTM1 deletion polymorphism affects detoxification capacity

enriched_entities.name: glutathione S-transferase pi 1
enriched_entities.function: Phase II detoxification enzyme; abundant in heart and other tissues; conjugates glutathione to xenobiotics and lipid peroxidation products
enriched_entities.role_in_context: PROTECTIVE - detoxifies doxorubicin and ROS-induced lipid peroxidation products. Upregulation provides cardioprotection
enriched_entities.clinical_relevance: GSTP1 polymorphisms may modulate doxorubicin toxicity

enriched_entities.name: ATP binding cassette subfamily B member 1
enriched_entities.function: ATP-dependent efflux pump; exports hydrophobic compounds including chemotherapy drugs from cells
enriched_entities.role_in_context: DUAL ROLE - protects normal tissues by limiting doxorubicin accumulation (cardioprotective), but also causes tumor drug resistance. Tissue-specific modulation could reduce toxicity while preserving tumor drug levels
enriched_entities.clinical_relevance: ABCB1 polymorphisms and expression levels affect doxorubicin pharmacokinetics and toxicity

enriched_entities.name: superoxide dismutase 2
enriched_entities.function: Mitochondrial antioxidant enzyme; converts superoxide radicals to hydrogen peroxide and oxygen
enriched_entities.role_in_context: PROTECTIVE - primary mitochondrial antioxidant defense; protects against doxorubicin-induced mitochondrial ROS and oxidative damage. SOD2 upregulation is cardioprotective
enriched_entities.clinical_relevance: SOD2 polymorphisms and expression levels modulate doxorubicin cardiotoxicity

enriched_entities.name: catalase
enriched_entities.function: Antioxidant enzyme; converts hydrogen peroxide to water and oxygen
enriched_entities.role_in_context: PROTECTIVE - scavenges H2O2 produced by SOD2 and other sources; protects against oxidative stress
enriched_entities.note: Not enriched due to tool budget; priority gene for Phase 3

enriched_entities.name: glutathione peroxidase 1
enriched_entities.function: Selenium-dependent antioxidant enzyme; reduces H2O2 and lipid hydroperoxides using glutathione
enriched_entities.role_in_context: PROTECTIVE - complements SOD2 and CAT in ROS scavenging; protects against oxidative damage
enriched_entities.note: Not enriched due to tool budget; priority gene for Phase 3

enriched_entities.name: DOXORUBICIN
enriched_entities.description: Anthracycline antibiotic; DNA intercalating agent and topoisomerase II poison
mechanisms: Stabilizes TOP2A-DNA and TOP2B-DNA cleavage complexes causing DNA damage
Generates reactive oxygen species via redox cycling
Intercalates into DNA disrupting replication and transcription

primary_targets.role: Primary anti-tumor target in proliferating cells

enriched_entities.note: ChEMBL API not called due to tool budget; using Phase 1 data

enriched_entities.name: Neurofibromatosis type 1
enriched_entities.description: Autosomal dominant tumor predisposition syndrome caused by loss-of-function mutations in NF1 gene; characterized by café-au-lait spots, neurofibromas, optic pathway gliomas, and increased risk of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors and other cancers
standard_treatments: Surgical resection of symptomatic neurofibromas and tumors
MEK inhibitors (selumetinib) for inoperable plexiform neurofibromas
Chemotherapy for malignant tumors (including doxorubicin-based regimens for MPNST)
Radiation therapy (limited use due to secondary malignancy risk)
enriched_entities.chemotherapy_considerations: NF1 patients with MPNST often receive doxorubicin-based chemotherapy but may have altered drug sensitivity due to RAS/MAPK pathway dysregulation. Cardiotoxicity monitoring is critical

disease_mechanism_rationale: NF1 is a tumor suppressor with loss-of-function mechanism causing disease. However, the question focuses on minimizing doxorubicin toxicity while preserving efficacy - this involves multiple genes with different mechanisms: TOP2B/CBR1 (toxicity mediators requiring inhibition/loss-of-function for protection), TOP2A (efficacy target requiring preservation), and antioxidant/detox genes (protective when upregulated/gain-of-function). The overall therapeutic strategy is context-dependent rather than single-mechanism
evidence: hgnc_get_gene provided cross-database IDs (HGNC → Ensembl, UniProt, Entrez) for NF1, TOP2B, TOP2A, CBR1, GSTM1, GSTP1, ABCB1, SOD2
Phase 1 literature context (PMIDs from doxorubicin cardiotoxicity and NF1 treatment searches) informed mechanism classification
TOP2B mechanism: doxorubicin-TOP2B cleavage complexes cause cardiotoxicity (loss-of-function protective)
TOP2A mechanism: doxorubicin-TOP2A cleavage complexes mediate anti-tumor efficacy (preserve function)
CBR1 mechanism: metabolizes doxorubicin to cardiotoxic doxorubicinol (loss-of-function protective)
GST genes (GSTM1, GSTP1): detoxify doxorubicin metabolites and ROS (gain-of-function protective)
SOD2: scavenges mitochondrial superoxide from doxorubicin (gain-of-function protective)
ABCB1: efflux pump with dual protective/resistance role
CAT and GPX1 identified as priority antioxidant genes but not enriched (tool budget limit)
